skip_summary: In 2026, a creator named The Architect built the AstroLink to connect the solar system, and the organization NETStart was formed to protect it. A massive solar storm suddenly strikes, destroying the communication panels at Earth headquarters. The Chief Astronaut arrives at an emergency meeting where Oberion, the leader of the Moon, explains that Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn have all lost connection. The Astronaut is tasked with traveling to each planet to fix the network, starting with an assessment on the Moon.

moon.1: The Astronaut lands safely on the Moon and touches down on the ground. They are greeted by the leader of the moon, Oberion, who introduces them to a short assessment and summons a figure named Nova. Nova is assigned to assist the Astronaut, evaluate their skills, and guide them to their upcoming objectives.
moon.2: Upon arriving at the landing bay, the Astronaut quickly spots the equipment they need for their upcoming interplanetary mission. The Astronaut instructs Nova to help pack their stuff so they can prepare to head to their next destination.
moon.3: The Astronaut asks Nova to double-check their bag, and Nova nods in confirmation that everything is perfectly complete. They board their spaceship, and the lights flare up to reveal colorful buttons. The Astronaut tells Nova to buckle up, but as they activate the engine, a warning sound emits from the system, declaring they have insufficient fuel for interplanetary travel.

mars.1: The spacecraft touches down on Mars, the planet in charge of marketing, where the duo is greeted by a chaotic scene of massive, completely blank, and disorganized planetary billboards. A friendly local resident named Mark approaches them, hoping they are the NETStart saviors sent to restore the connection. Mark explains that when the solar storm hit, the billboards flickered and went blank, leaving the planet without a solution.
mars.2: After fixing the first billboard, Mark leaves with gratitude, and Nova summarizes that the storm's network shutdown caused the blackout. Suddenly, two identical creatures, twins Emma G. and Penny G., interrupt them and confirm that the storm knocked the AstroLink offline. The twins point out that embedded visual videos on the billboard are still broken due to the downed connection, and they offer to lead the duo directly to the main Martian AstroLink.
mars.3: Arriving at the location of the downed AstroLink, the Astronaut pulls the necessary replacement parts from their bag and prepares to permanently fix the communication device and the final broken billboard.

venus.1: Approaching Venus, the Astronaut notices the planet looks starkly black and white, as if trapped in a retro film. They receive a frantic video transmission from Professor Spectrum, who directs them to his laboratory. Spectrum explains that the solar storm completely drained the planet into a monochromatic state and vanished the AstroLink device. Without a backup, they look out at a transparent gap in space and realize they must build a replacement from scratch to restore the foundational borders and colors.
venus.2: The newly built prototype synthesizes the missing colors and borders, bringing a splash of color back to the lab. However, Professor Spectrum notes the model still generates chaotic, disorganized signals. The team heads to the massive maintenance room to format the prototype, realizing its layout looks vastly different from the original dormant AstroLink hardware and must be properly aligned before it can be plugged in.
venus.3: Professor Hue bursts into the room to announce the AstroLink is technically back online, but looking at the horizon, the team realizes sprawling patches of the landscape remain stubbornly trapped in black and white due to a weak connection. Professor Spectrum determines they must fully integrate their newly built CSS prototype with the main HTML network to amplify the system and fix the remaining dead zones.

mercury.1: Arriving at Mercury, the central supply hub for every planet, the duo notices an unusual stillness because all interplanetary transport is on strict hiatus. They hear a distressed voice and find Professor Dominic, the head botanist, frantically pacing over withered plants. Dominic explains the solar storm completely fried the biodome's terminal, causing the environment and plant life to collapse.
mercury.2: Once the biodome is restored and the flora regains its vibrant color, Dominic's celebration is cut short by a frantic buzz from his pocket. He learns the storm melted the logic boards on the AstroLink factory's main conveyor belt, leaving them unable to route incoming materials. Dominic rushes the duo inside the cavernous factory to fix the jammed tracks and properly sort the shipments.
mercury.3: Dominic inspects the main communication relay and notes the hardware is functioning perfectly, but they still cannot receive incoming planetary data. Nova analyzes the system and realizes the electromagnetic surge from the storm wiped the entire front-end software interface, meaning the Astronaut must rebuild the messaging interface from scratch.

jupiter.1: Approaching Jupiter's swirling storms, Nova notes they can land on the outer platforms, but a colossal barrier gate seals off the main entry point into Jupiter. The Astronaut enters their access codes into the airlock terminal, but it flashes a bright warning, declaring them as unfamiliar intruders and keeping the heavy doors tightly shut.
jupiter.2: Once they bypass the gate, the door hisses open to reveal the cloud grid chamber, where they meet Technician Io. Io explains she has been locked inside for two days because the storm scrambled the data grid, causing the security system to treat everyone as an intruder. The main server keeps reading corrupted data blocks and crashing, so the Astronaut creates a safety net to quarantine the bad data safely without triggering a fatal error.
jupiter.3: Entering the empty main vault, the floating AI Core denies them access, keeping threat protocols active because it doesn't recognize outside signals post-storm. Nova realizes the AI isn't glitching but simply lacks a blueprint to trust them, prompting the Astronaut to begin creating a brand-new authorized role profile with access codes baked in to convince the AI they aren't a threat.

saturn.1: Arriving at Saturn, Nova and the Astronaut immediately notice the celestial ringworld is completely motionless. Landing at the main control panel, they are greeted by a worn-out Lead Systems Technician named Engineer Titan. Titan explains that the storm-fed garbage data has entered the sensor array and tripped the failover logic, meaning the terminal is storing data in the wrong containers and needs its power routing commands manually inputted.
saturn.2: With power restored, Titan takes them to the observation deck, revealing the rings are completely jammed by thousands of loose debris fragments, including ice, rock, and scrap metal. Because different materials require different handling, the Astronaut devises a clean matching system that automatically identifies and sorts the debris to quickly jumpstart each individual ring sector.
saturn.3: The massive ring sectors shudder and return to their majestic spinning orbit, but a shrill alarm suddenly blares as the system begins crashing again. Nova realizes a massive memory leak is occurring in the core processing bay because the restarted systems are borrowing memory but never returning it, forcing the team to sprint down to fix the core pattern.

earth_not_last.1: The Astronaut is caught completely by surprise when Oberion calls and orders them back to Earth immediately for an emergency. Upon landing, Oberion reveals the Master Ledger, the only record of planetary statuses, went dark without any storm warning. In the main control room, Director Atlas shows them a screen full of scattered, mismatched data, and the Astronaut promises to rebuild the ledger line by line.
earth_not_last.2: Atlas asks for a single, structured file where every planet's information lives together so it can be searched instantly. As they organize the scattered facts into a clean archive, they discover a mysterious active entry from "Row zero" labeled "The Architect's Wing." Oberion admits this wing hasn't been on any map since the Architect disappeared, and Nova suggests they go find him since he's been sending data this whole time.
earth_not_last.3: The sealed door opens to a small room with no person, only a soft hum and a voice from the computer screen. The Architect reveals that he merged his mind with the network years ago and accidentally broke the system when he panicked and tried to connect Uranus and Neptune too early. He admits he has been quietly holding what is left together on his own, hoping NETStart could fix the rest without ever finding this room.

earth_last.1: After weeks of chasing signals across the solar system, the Astronaut returns to Earth, noting that five planetary signals now blink a steady green while Earth remains a dull gray. Oberion meets them on the landing pad in person, praising their incredible work but warning that the hardest part of the mission is waiting right here at the center. Inside the control room, Director Atlas explains the Master Ledger is completely scrambled, and the Astronaut sets to work rebuilding the chaotic data.
earth_last.2: Atlas asks for a single, structured file where every planet's information lives together so it can be searched instantly. As they organize the scattered facts into a clean archive, they discover a mysterious active entry from "Row zero" labeled "The Architect's Wing." Oberion admits this wing hasn't been on any map since the Architect disappeared, and Nova suggests they go find him since he's been sending data this whole time.
earth_last.3: Inside the sealed wing, they discover a small room with only a computer screen, where the Architect reveals he merged his mind with the network and accidentally broke the system by panicking and trying to connect Uranus and Neptune before the network was strong enough. The Architect admits he has one final program left to run that will tie all their planetary repairs together, and he asks the Astronaut if they will run it with him.
